1	# Remote-sensing inputs that set the solar-wind ion flux at 3I/ATLAS during XMM (2025-12-03T12:04 to 12-04T10:12 UT)
2	
3	Scope: the leading-order inputs for the ion flux nv at one point near 1.87 AU over about one day, and how each should enter a WSA + MHD (ENLIL- or EUHFORIA-like) chain. The data files are described in `README_remote_sensing.md`. The numbers below come from `qc/comet_source_mapping.csv`, `qc/data_age_20251125.csv` and `cme/cme_comet_geometry.csv`.
4	
5	## 0. Geometry that drives the ranking
6	
7	- **Comet during XMM** (Horizons JPL#54): r = 1.862 to 1.885 AU, HEEQ longitude +75.9° to +74.4°, HEEQ latitude −6.4°, Earth-view Carrington longitude 30° to 16°.
8	- **Other observers:**
9	  - STEREO-A: +50.1°, 0.967 AU, latitude −5.3°.
10	  - Solar Orbiter: +14.6°, 0.90 AU, latitude +9.5°.
11	  - PSP: −78°.
12	- **Ballistic source of the plasma at the comet** (arrival in the XMM window, 300 to 700 km/s, sidereal rate 14.18°/day):
13	  - Departures from the Sun fall between 2025-11-22.8 and 11-29.8.
14	  - Source Carrington longitudes are 83° to 183°.
15	  - At departure each source sat 79° to 87° west of Earth's central meridian (CM), near the west limb as seen from Earth.
16	  - Each source last crossed Earth's CM 6.0 to 6.6 d before departure, which is 10.6 to 17.3 d before the XMM window.
17	  - A model driven by one frozen map at the XMM epoch therefore uses data 11 to 17 d old for these longitudes, which by then are 140° to 230° from Earth's CM (far side).

42	- **GONG mrzqs** (zero-point-corrected QR hourly synoptic): `https://gong.nso.edu/data/magmap/QR/zqs/`.
43	  - It is the WSA 5.4 input at CCMC/iSWA. Each WSA header has `FILELIST=mrzql...`, the matching product.
44	  - The data are 360×180 sine-latitude. The left edge is at CM − 60°, and those 60° have not yet crossed CM.
45	  - It is weighted by cos⁴ of the central-meridian distance (CMD), so at any longitude it is dominated by observations within about ±30° of CM.
46	  - In Nov 2025 it updated normally.
47	- **ADAPT-GONG** (Arge et al. 2010; Hickmann et al. 2015): `https://gong.nso.edu/adapt/maps/gong/`.
48	  - It is a 12-realization flux-transport model with enLS assimilation.
49	  - **The archived run has no assimilation between 2025-10-08 15:04 and 2025-11-18 ~22 UT.** `LAST_OBS` reaches 40.4 d, and the files were rewritten 2026-03-02.
50	  - On 25 Nov the ADAPT map is fresh only over longitudes ~0-150°. Longitudes 150-360° carry evolved early-October flux: in the STDDEV map they show 47-75 d data age and high σ. Mid-November active regions at 230-290° that GONG saw are missing (`qc/maps_gong_adapt_20251125.png`).

60	## 3. WSA and inner-boundary prescriptions
61	
62	**WSA velocity law, as run at CCMC/iSWA (WSA v5.4, GONGz and ADAPT, evaluated at 21.5 Rs).** It is taken verbatim from the `VELEQN` header of the iSWA `vel_*_gongz.fits` files:
63	
64	  v = 285 + 625 / (1 + f_s)^(2/9) × [1 − 0.8 exp(−(θ_b / 2°)²)]³ km/s
65	
66	- f_s is the expansion factor at RADSS = 2.51 Rs (WSA plane 2). θ_b is the footpoint distance to the coronal-hole boundary in degrees (plane 6).
67	- Evaluating the law on those two planes reproduces the archived speed plane exactly.
68	- The model is PFSS to 2.51 Rs plus a Schatten current sheet from 2.49 Rs, with 90 harmonics and scaled monopole correction.
69	- No published description of the v5.x coefficients was found. They match Reiss et al. 2019 (ApJS 240, 35, Eq. 12: v0 = 285, v1 − v0 = 625, α = 2/9, β = 1, γ = 0.8, w = 2), except that Reiss prints δ = 3 where the header has 2.
70	- The ENLIL run uses this product directly (`cordata=wsadw_5.4`, `corona=WSA_V5.4`). CCMC retired WSA 5.4 from its continuous runs on 2025-12-08; the archive stays on iSWA.
71	
72	**Other calibrations.** Items marked UNVERIFIED were not re-checked against the primary source here.
73	- **Arge et al. 2003/2004:** the original fs-θb forms. Coefficients UNVERIFIED. Edwards et al. 2015 (Solar Phys. 290, 2791) quote the Arge 2004 variant as 240 + 675/(1+f_s)^(1/4.5)·[1 − 0.8 exp(−(θ_b/1.9°)²)]³.
74	- **McGregor et al. 2011 (JGR 116, A03101):** form 240 + 675/(1+f_s)^(2/9)·[1 − 0.8 exp(−(θ_b/w)^β)]³. The values w ≈ 2.8° and β = 1.25 are commonly attributed to this paper; UNVERIFIED.
75	- **Riley et al. 2015 (Space Weather 13, 154):** shows that θ_b (distance from the coronal-hole boundary) carries most of the skill and f_s adds little. Coefficients UNVERIFIED.
76	- **Reiss et al. 2020 (ApJ 891, 165):** eight coefficients with defaults c1..c8 = 250, 650, 0.29, 1, 0.8, 3°, 1.75, 3.
77	  - The output is most sensitive to c4 > c1 > c3 > c2.
78	  - Per-rotation adaptive selection improves RMSE from 111 to 94 km/s at Earth.
79	  - Implication for us: treat the coefficients as uncertain at the ±4% level for c1-c4. That is about ±40 km/s, or roughly ±0.3 d in stream timing at 1.9 AU.
80	
81	**ENLIL 2.8f "a6b1" inner boundary at 0.1 AU.** These are the values used in the reviewer's run, from its netCDF attribute `boundary_old = "B=350./4./0./1 D=125./2. T=1.5/0 V=700./25./75./200. S=9. A=0.05"`. They agree with the CCMC run metadata (e.g. Lan_Jian_112717_SH_1).
82	- vfast = 700 and vslow = 200 km/s. vrfast = 25 and vrslow = 75 km/s are the reductions of the maximum and minimum WSA speeds.
83	- Density: n = dfast (vfast/v)², with dfast = 125 cm⁻³. This keeps momentum flux constant, nv² = const (Odstrcil et al. 2020, ApJS 246, 73).
84	- Temperature: T = tfast · dfast/n = 1.5 MK (v/vfast)², so thermal pressure nT is constant.
85	- Field: Br = bscl × WSA Br, with bscl = 4 (the GONG default) and bfast = 350 nT. Bφ comes from corotation (synodic frame).
86	- Alpha fraction xalpha = 0.05. Polytropic index g53q5 is γ = 5/3 with heating; the "q5" detail is UNVERIFIED.
87	- CME clouds, d4t1x1: density 4× the fast stream, temperature 1× the fast stream, spheroid (`ncld=2`), no cavity.
88	- Check: v = 400 km/s at 0.1 AU gives n = 383 cm⁻³, which scales to 1.10 cm⁻³ at 1.87 AU. That matches the run's 1.0-1.1 cm⁻³ at the comet.
89	- Other settings use other references, for example a3b2 (vfast 675, dfast 200, tfast 0.8 MK) and Odstrcil et al. 2020's reference fast wind (200 cm⁻³, 1 MK, 700 km/s).
90	
91	**EUHFORIA (Pomoell & Poedts 2018, JSWSC 8, A35).** Values as summarized by Hinterreiter et al. 2019 and Samara et al. 2024:
92	
93	  v = 240 + 675/(1+f)^0.222 × [1 − 0.8 exp(−(d/w)^1.25)]³ km/s, with w = 0.02 rad (d is the angular distance to the coronal-hole boundary)
94	
95	- Then 50 km/s is subtracted and v is bounded to 275-625 km/s.
96	- Density: n = n_fsw (v_fsw/v)², with n_fsw = 300 cm⁻³ and v_fsw = 675 km/s.
97	- Temperature: T = T_fsw ρ_fsw/ρ, with T_fsw = 0.8 MK, so thermal pressure is constant at about 3.3 nPa.
98	- Field: B_r = sgn(B_corona) B_fsw (v/v_fsw), with B_fsw = 300 nT. This is the open-flux normalization, independent of the PFSS |B|.
99	- The PSP-calibrated variant of Samara et al. 2024 (V0 = 207, V1 = 725, w = 0.031 rad, β = 0.50) did worse at Earth.
100	
101	**Consequence for flux.** At a given boundary speed, nv at 0.1 AU is n_f v_f²/v. EUHFORIA's (300 cm⁻³, 675 km/s) is 2.2× ENLIL a6b1's (125 cm⁻³, 700 km/s), and the WSA law plus offset sets v. The density reference is therefore the largest single free constant for the absolute ion flux at the comet. It must be calibrated in situ, at STEREO-A first.

139	## 6. Assimilation and calibration
140	
141	- **BRaVDA (Lang & Owens 2019, Space Weather 17, 59):** a variational assimilation of in-situ speeds into a reduced-physics, HUX-type outward propagation. Applied to STEREO-A/B data from Oct 2010 to Oct 2011, it improved near-Earth speed in 12 of 13 rotations, cutting RMSE by about 18%.
142	- **Lang et al. 2021 (Space Weather 19, e2020SW002698):** BRaVDA with HUXt, the boundary updated at 30 Rs, assimilating STEREO-A, STEREO-B and ACE over 2007-2014. RMSE falls by about one third, and the latitude bias goes away.
143	- **Turner et al. 2023 (Space Weather 21, e2023SW003457):** near-real-time STEREO plus ACE/DSCOVR inputs perform about as well as science data, with speed mean absolute error down about 46%.
144	- **For 3I/ATLAS:**
145	  - Assimilate STEREO-A PLASTIC speed (HEEQ +50°, 26° upstream of the comet in corotation, with a lag of about 5.5 d), ACE/Wind and Solar Orbiter (+15°) over Nov 10 to Dec 10.
146	  - Ballistically, the plasma that reaches the comet mid-XMM passed the same source longitudes at STEREO-A between Nov 26.3 (300 km/s) and Nov 29.6 (700 km/s). That is a lag of 4.4-7.6 d, and STEREO-A sits at nearly the comet's latitude (−5.3° vs −6.4°), so the comet's source band is directly constrained.
147	  - **Caveat:** the Nov 23 CME shock reached STEREO-A at Nov 26.8, inside this sampling interval. Those STEREO-A data are therefore not purely ambient, and the ICME must be masked or modeled before they are assimilated.
148	  - Then use the posterior v(φ) at 0.1 AU, plus a calibrated n_f, as the MHD boundary.
149	- **WSA coefficient calibration** (Reiss et al. 2019/2020): an ensemble over c1-c4 (±4%) and over the 12 ADAPT realizations gives the boundary-speed prior that assimilation then narrows.

151	## 7. What to do in our model
152	
153	1. Drive the 0.1 AU boundary hourly or daily from the WSA 5.4 GONGz maps (identical timestamps to the CCMC run) and, separately, from the 12 ADAPT-WSA realizations. Compute v from planes 2 and 6 with the law above, and take Br from plane 1. Treat the GONG-vs-ADAPT difference as a systematic.
154	2. Calibrate the boundary density and temperature (n_f, T_f) and the WSA offsets against STEREO-A over 15 Nov-10 Dec, with Wind and SolO as checks. Then report nv at the comet as a range over the ensemble.
155	3. Run with and without the Nov 23 CME pair, constrained by the STEREO-A shock at 2025-11-26T18:48. Their trailing effects may dominate the deviation from ambient during XMM.
156	4. Use EUVI 195 coronal-hole boundaries near Carrington longitudes 100-180°, observed Nov 20-28, to choose between maps or realizations where the WSA θb disagrees.

Downloaded 2026-10-16/17. Everything here is public and needs no account. Total size is about 300 MB. The scripts live in `scripts_rs/` and run as `python -I scripts_rs/<name>.py` (sunpy env: `/home/scabot/miniconda3/envs/mhd_claude/bin/python`):

| script | what it does |
|---|---|
| `fetch_maps.py gong adapt wsa wsavel wsaadapt ensemble` | daily map downloads, one file per day closest to 00 UT (within ±12 h), 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-06 |
| `index_maps.py` | writes the `index.csv` files from the FITS headers |
| `ephem_heeq.py` | JPL Horizons vectors (Sun-centered ICRF) converted to HEEQ (HGS) and Earth-view Carrington longitude, 3-hourly from 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-12 |

## 1. GONG mrzqs (`gong/`, 53 files, 13 MB)

- Source: `https://gong.nso.edu/data/magmap/QR/zqs/YYYYMM/mrzqsYYMMDD/mrzqsYYMMDDtHHMMcCRRR_LLL.fits.gz`. This is the hourly, zero-point-corrected, QuickReduce (QR) standard synoptic map. `LLL` in the name is the left-edge longitude.
- Layout: a single primary HDU of 360 x 180 float32 in Gauss. It is Carrington cylindrical equal-area, so axis 2 is sine(latitude) with `CDELT2 = 1/90`. Pixel-center longitude is `CRVAL1 + (i+1-CRPIX1)*CDELT1` (0-based i), which runs from `LONG0 + 0.5` to `LONG0 + 359.5`. The map is not wrapped to 0-360.
- Time and longitude keywords:
  - `MAPDATE`/`MAPTIME`: the UT of the last contributing magnetogram.
  - `CAR_ROT`: the rotation of longitude 0 of the map.
  - `MAPL0`: the Earth central-meridian (CM) longitude at map time.
  - `LONG0` = `MAPEDGE`: the left (leading) edge longitude, which is 60° east of CM.
  - `CRNOW` and `CR60`: fractional Carrington-rotation numbers for "now" and for the point 60° in.
  - `CRVAL1A`/`CDELT1A`: the fractional-rotation axis.
  - Following the header COMMENT, the 60° of the map to the left of `MAPL0` has not yet crossed CM.
- `index.csv` columns: file, map_time_utc, carrington_rotation, cr_lon_at_map_time (= MAPL0), crnow, left_edge_lon, nfiles, image_mean_G.
- Gaps: none at daily cadence. The nearest-to-00 UT pick is the previous day's 23:24/23:34 file for 2025-11-19, 11-21 and 12-04, and 2025-10-14 21:14 for 2025-10-15.
- `FILELIST` in each mrzqs header points to the matching `mrzql` file. WSA reads that file, as the WSA headers below show.

## 2. ADAPT-GONG (`adapt/`, 53 files, 158 MB)

- Source: `https://gong.nso.edu/adapt/maps/gong/2025/adapt40311_044012_YYYYMMDD0000_<lastobs>.fts.gz`. All of these are the 00 UT maps. The naming follows the NSO ADAPT readme:
  - `4`: public.
  - `0`: Carrington-fixed frame. A twin `adapt41311` series uses the CM-centered frame.
  - `3`: GONG input.
  - `1`: enLS data assimilation.
  - `1`: 1° resolution.
  - `04 4`: code version.
  - `012`: realizations.
  - The tail `TIIJJKKLLGQ` gives the evolution mode and the time since the last assimilated observation.
- Layout: HDU0 is (12, 180, 360) float32 in Gauss, one plane per realization. Latitude is equal-angle, from -89.5 to 89.5. Longitude is Carrington-fixed with pixel centers 0.5 to 359.5 (`CRVAL1=180` at `CRPIX1=180.5`). The other HDUs are:
  - HDU1 `ensemParmInfo`: per-realization supergranulation, meridional-flow, differential-rotation and random-flux parameters.
  - HDU2/3: ensemble statistics.
  - HDU4 `STDDEV`: the 12-member standard-deviation map.
- Keywords:
  - `MAPTIME`, `MAPJUL`.
  - `MAPLON`/`MAPCR`: CM longitude and rotation at map time.
  - `LAST_OBS`: days since the last assimilated magnetogram.
  - `NREAL`, `COVERAGE`.
  - `FLUXSCAL = 1.8`: a scaling applied to the input GONG data.
  - `CRLNGEDG`/`CRROTEDG`: the WSA leading edge.
- `index.csv` columns: file, map_time_utc, carrington_rotation, map_cr, cr_lon_at_map_time, nreal, last_obs_days, coverage_pct, fluxscal, modelver.
- **Major caveat:** the archived ADAPT-GONG run assimilated no data from 2025-10-08 15:04 UT to 2025-11-18 ~22 UT. `LAST_OBS` climbs from 6.4 d on Oct 15 to 40.4 d on Nov 18, then resets to 0.09 d on Nov 19. The `adapt41311` twin has the same tags. The NSO files were rewritten on 2026-03-02, and GONG mrzqs kept updating normally over that interval.
  - Consequence: on 2025-11-25 the ADAPT maps hold fresh data only over roughly 0-150° Carrington longitude. That is the disk seen since Nov 19; the STDDEV plane shows it as a low-variance disk. Longitudes ~150-360° hold flux-transported data from before Oct 8, about 47-75 days old.
  - In the GONG map the same far-side longitudes show active regions observed in mid-November (lon 230-290). The two inputs will give different global PFSS/HCS solutions.
  - The real-time iSWA ADAPT-WSA outputs (below) were computed in Nov 2025 from the ADAPT run as it stood then, which is not the archived run. I compared photospheric Br at |lat| < 50° on 2025-11-25:
    - Over the stale longitudes 190-330°, real-time ADAPT-WSA plane 5 correlates r = 0.26 with archived ADAPT and r = 0.41 with mrzqs. Archived ADAPT against mrzqs gives r = 0.12, and GONGz-WSA against mrzqs gives r = 0.92.
    - Over the fresh longitudes 10-140°, the correlations are 0.92, 0.85, 0.78 and 0.89 respectively.
    - So the real-time run was at least partly fed during the gap, and the archived files should not be used for boundary dates before Nov 19 or for far-side structure through about Dec 10.
